figures.finding: The Bahamas levies no income tax on individuals, so a resident's pay and fees bear none.

sources.said: Individual taxation There is no individual income tax.
There are no compliance requirements for individuals, as there is no individual income tax.

figures.finding: A non-resident performer's or writer's fee bears no income tax or withholding in The Bahamas; there is no withholding on royalties or service fees.

sources.said: There is no withholding tax on dividends, interest, royalties, or technical service fees, and no branch remittance tax.

figures.finding: National insurance: the employer pays 6.65% and the employee 4.65% of wages up to BSD 3,510 a month (BSD 810 a week); the self-employed pay 10.3% of average insurable income to the same ceiling.
figures.applies: Employees and self-employed people registered with the National Insurance Board.

sources.said: Employers are required to pay 6.65% of employees’ wages, with a maximum wage ceiling of BSD 3,510 monthly or BSD 810 weekly. Individuals are also required to register with the National Insurance Board. Employees must contribute 4.65% of wages, up to the maximum wage ceiling. Self-employed individuals are subject to a rate of 10.3% of average insurable income, with a maximum ceiling of BSD 3,510 monthly or BSD 810 weekly.

figures.finding: A freelancer must register for and charge VAT once past or expected 12-month taxable activity exceeds BSD 100,000; the standard rate is 10%.
figures.applies: Taxable supplies in The Bahamas (VAT Act); registration within 14 days.

sources.said: You are required to register for and charge VAT under the VAT Act if your past or future 12 months of taxable activity exceeds the $100,000 threshold. Most businesses must apply within 14 days of meeting these requirements or face penalties.
The standard rate of VAT for most goods and services is 10%.
Two rates of VAT are applied which is the standard rate of 10% and a zero rate of 0%.

sources.title: Bahamas Highlights 2026 (Deloitte International Tax)
sources.said: Individual taxation There is no individual income tax. … There are no compliance requirements for individuals, as there is no individual income tax. … There is no withholding tax on dividends, interest, royalties, or technical service fees, and no branch remittance tax. … Employers are required to pay 6.65% of employees’ wages, with a maximum wage ceiling of BSD 3,510 monthly or BSD 810 weekly. Individuals are also required to register with the National Insurance Board. Employees must contribute 4.65% of wages, up to the maximum wage ceiling. Self-employed individuals are subject to a rate of 10.3% of average insurable income, with a maximum ceiling of BSD 3,510 monthly or BSD 810 weekly.

sources.title: Value Added Tax – FAQs (Department of Inland Revenue)
sources.said: You are required to register for and charge VAT under the VAT Act if your past or future 12 months of taxable activity exceeds the $100,000 threshold. Most businesses must apply within 14 days of meeting these requirements or face penalties. … The standard rate of VAT for most goods and services is 10%.

sources.title: About VAT (Department of Inland Revenue)
sources.said: Two rates of VAT are applied which is the standard rate of 10% and a zero rate of 0%.
